purpose: Provide bounded coordinated X/Y separation-choice search for the coupled failures diagnosed in 2026-10-12-separation-cycle-geometry.json. Kernel only: not enabled in production placement yet.

implementation.input: Explicit finite alternatives for each named movable/movable or movable/fixed pair, with caller-supplied axis, endpoint order and directional gap. First alternative is the incumbent. Additional hard difference constraints are immutable.
implementation.algorithm: Deterministic breadth-first search of distinct complete choice assignments. Solve X, then Y against the SAME assignment with all automatic axis flips disabled. On an actual negative cycle, branch on every alternative of its implicated separation domains. Never remove a wall or additional hard edge. A hard-only cycle closes that assignment.
implementation.cycle_provenance: RepairAxisResult now includes stable input separation indices parallel to the actual terminal cycle witness. The new kernel does not parse diagnostic names to decide which constraints to change.
implementation.bounds: Positive max_states caps GENERATED distinct assignments, including the initial state, bounding both the pending queue and visited set. Already queued assignments are still explored when the cap is hit. At most two axis solves per visited assignment. Limits above size_t max/2 are rejected to prevent probe-count wrap. This is not a wall-time bound.
implementation.result: Return the first two-axis feasible proposal and its choices, or no poses on failure. A fully exhausted finite-domain failure is distinct from budget exhaustion. Axis feasibility uses the existing Bellman-Ford numerical tolerance; results require independent physical, nonlinear hard-term and output-grid checks before any acceptance.
implementation.validation: Reject malformed dimensions, names, pair domains, additional edges, nonfinite geometry and nonfinite derived constraints/solver positions. Opposite-direction gaps are explicit inputs, never inferred by reusing another direction's gap.
implementation.work_receipts: Generated-state, visited-state, actual axis-solve and budget counts are returned. An optional invocation-owned trivial work receipt is updated even during exception unwinding, without publishing speculative geometry or storing a shared sink.

tests.independent_oracle: Twenty-five integer board sizes, two 2x2 movable rectangles and a fixed 2x2 obstacle, with three four-direction pair domains. Exhaustively enumerate integer coordinates independently of the cycle search and require complete-domain results to agree. Every accepted proposal independently satisfies walls, pair clearances and its selected directed inequalities.
tests.determinism: Repeat every query and compare outcome, coordinates, choices and all work counters.
tests.adversarial: Direction-specific 1/3/5 mm alternatives require a reversed Y branch; a tightened bound proves a smaller reused gap would incorrectly accept. Test a hard-only negative cycle, zero-work invalid inputs, untouched feasible incumbent, unknown names, empty domains, overflow, infinity/NaN, generated-state cap and counter overflow protection.
tests.exception_receipt: A derived-edge overflow after preparing the initial state reports generated=1, visited=1, axis_solves=0. A subsequent invalid zero-budget call replaces that receipt with zero work.
tests.reference_scope: The floorplan suite includes both carrier and devkit frozen floorplan/estimator regressions. No new full-board build, render or timing comparison is claimed.

integration_requirements: Construct every permitted orientation using current face-aware child geometry and directional fanout/channel gaps; never mirror gaps blindly. Preserve existing successful placements. Attach actual retry and work receipts. Qualify proposals through all current output-grid, exact physical and hard-term checks, and consider bounded continuation if the first linear proposal fails those checks. Only then screen the carrier and independently qualify a promising finalist. No policy ratchet or acceptance gate changed.
status: Tested search foundation, not a completed smaller-board solution or whole-goal completion. Production search policy remains unchanged; routing and fabrication readiness are not claimed.
